header.hide_bar_title: Hide main bar (show it again with the button in the toolbar)

library.title: Organ Library
library.empty_title: No organs in the library yet.
library.empty_hint: Use the buttons in the top right to load an organ.
library.download_where: Choose the folder where the sample set will be stored
library.choose_image_title: Choose a photo of the organ

settings.audio_latency_hint: For low latency: choose an ASIO driver (e.g. ASIO4ALL) or an audio interface. WASAPI shared mode adds ~20-40 ms; ASIO ~5-12 ms. Buffer size only applies to ASIO — WASAPI ignores it. ASIO requires a separate build (see BUILDING.md).
settings.audio_asio_hint: ASIO exposes only one device. Want to pick a specific headphone or speaker? Open the ASIO panel (e.g. ASIO4ALL) to set the output, or switch to WASAPI above to choose each output separately.
settings.sampleset_no_organ: Load an organ first to check its samples.
settings.sampleset_desc: Detects and trims silence before the attack from the loaded organ's samples. Originals are backed up to a '_backup' folder first; the files are then overwritten.
settings.sampleset_busy: Working… this may take a while.
settings.sampleset_confirm: Originals will be backed up first, then the samples overwritten. Continue?
settings.midi_bluetooth_help: No BLE MIDI devices found. Click 'Scan' to search.
settings.midi_bluetooth_help_text: Make sure your BLE MIDI device is on and in pairing mode.
settings.sample_rate_hint: The rate follows the default Windows audio device. For 96 kHz or higher: set this via Windows Sound Settings → Properties → Advanced → Default Format, and restart JM-Orgue.
settings.wind_groups_hint: Assign each division to a group (in the MIDI mapping below). Two divisions in the same group share one wind reservoir.
settings.temperament_original_hint: Original: the samples sound as recorded (sample-set PitchTuning applied, no retuning).
settings.temperament_retune_hint: Retuning: every pipe is tuned from its measured pitch to the selected temperament (as in GrandOrgue); celestes keep their intended detuning.
settings.temperament_measured: This set has measured pipe pitches ({n} of {total} pipes).
settings.temperament_no_measured: No measured pipe pitches in this set — 'Equal temperament' sounds the same as 'Original'; other temperaments are applied as offsets on the recording.
settings.tremulant_from_samples: From the recording: this sample set has real tremulant recordings. The simulation is not needed on top.
settings.tremulant_simulated: Simulated: this sample set contains no tremulant recordings, so the tremulant is computed here.
settings.appearance_subtitle: Freely adjust colors, font and background, or pick a preset
settings.panel_close_quits: Closing an extra screen closes the whole application
settings.panel_close_quits_title: On: the close button on an extra screen quits JM-Orgue entirely (handy on an organ console). Off: only that screen closes; the organ keeps playing.
settings.output_pair_hint: Which two outputs of the currently open audio output all divisions use (e.g. outputs 3–4 of an 8-channel interface). Per-division routing is under MIDI Channel per Keyboard → Outputs; this then shows "Per division (custom)".
settings.test_signal_hint: Click a channel number to send sound there — that tells you which plug goes to which speaker. Click again to stop; it also stops when you leave this screen.
settings.polyphony_hint: Maximum number of simultaneously sounding pipes incl. release tails. Higher = more CPU on one core; keep the load below ~80%.
settings.stereo_samples_hint: On: stereo recordings keep their spatial image (more memory). Off: mix down to mono as before.
settings.reload_hint: Takes effect after reloading the organ.
settings.channels_per_division_hint: Choose which outputs of the currently open audio output ({host}) this division uses — from 1 up to all. Two consecutive outputs form a stereo pair; a single output plays mono. The count follows the device: ASIO exposes all driver outputs, WASAPI the number Windows has configured for this device.
settings.channel_out_of_range: output not present on this device → plays on 1–2
settings.channel_partly_out_of_range: output {list} not present on this device; only the remaining chosen outputs play
settings.channel_out_of_range_hint: This division is set to an output the currently open device does not have (e.g. 3–4 after switching to stereo headphones). Pick other outputs here or switch back to the multichannel device.
settings.audio_channels_available: {n} outputs available on the currently open audio output ({host})
settings.audio_channels_hint: The number of outputs is that of the audio output currently playing. ASIO exposes all outputs of the driver (e.g. 8 on an 8-channel interface). WASAPI exposes the number Windows has configured for this device (Settings → System → Sound → device → speaker setup; 7.1 = 8).
settings.audio_channels_hint_wasapi: If Windows shows the interface as separate stereo devices, choose ASIO to get all outputs at once.
settings.audio_latency_driver_default: latency: driver default (WASAPI ≈ 20–30 ms; choose ASIO + a small buffer for less)
settings.autosave_hint: Settings are saved automatically in the organ folder and in the app.
settings.short_octave_title: Historic keyboard with an incomplete bottom octave: the key that looks like E sounds C, F# sounds D and G# sounds E. C# and D# are missing there.
settings.short_octave_needs_range: Learn the key range first (or fill in the lowest note): without the lowest key the app cannot tell where the bottom octave starts.
settings.midi_key_range_title: Manual key range: lowest and highest MIDI note (alternative to 'Learn'). Empty = no limit.
settings.tremulant_enable_title: Make the tremulant available on this keyboard — a Tremulant stop then appears in the organ view
settings.audio_profiles_desc: Save two output setups (e.g. speakers via ASIO and headphones via WASAPI — or the same ASIO interface with different channels). The per-keyboard channel selection (the "Outputs" checkboxes under MIDI Channel per Keyboard) is stored in the profile and switches along with it. Then switch with one button in the top bar — or via a learned MIDI button. First choose host, device, buffer and channels, then save.
settings.audio_profile_save_title: Save the current selection (host/device/buffer + per-keyboard channel choice) as the {name} profile
settings.audio_profile_activate_title: Switch to this profile now (also to rebuild a stuttering output)
settings.audio_profile_learn_title: MIDI learn for the speakers/headphones switch ({n}/4)
settings.loops_desc: Detects a good sustain loop per WAV (fundamental period, phase-aligned), bakes in a crossfade for a seamless transition and writes the loop points into the file (smpl chunk). For samplesets without loops, so that notes keep sounding. Originals are backed up first.
settings.audio_buffer_hint: Smaller = less latency, but the audio thread has to do all the work of a stop or crescendo change within that time. 128 frames (2.7 ms) is the right choice on almost any PC; 32/48 only on a very fast PC without reverb.

perspectives.keep_loaded_title: Then you switch recording position instantly while playing instead of reloading the organ. Costs memory: roughly times the number of positions.
perspectives.title: Perspectives and stacked ranks
perspectives.desc: This sample set has several microphone positions. Choose which ones to load (uses memory) and mix them per position.
perspectives.stacked_note: {n} stops consist of several ranks (e.g. mixtures); those always sound in full.
perspectives.reload_hint: The choice of loaded perspectives takes effect after reloading the organ.
perspectives.none: This organ has a single perspective.

midi_player.title: Play MIDI
midi_player.subtitle: Play a .mid file through the organ

voicing.title: Pipe voicing
voicing.subtitle: Adjust volume and tuning per individual pipe
voicing.choose_register: Pick a stop on the left to voice.

register_panel.select_from_library: Select an organ from the library

status_bar.load_title: Sounding voices / polyphony limit · audio thread load
status_bar.archiving_title: The automatic MIDI archive is capturing your playing; the file is saved after the silence period.
status_bar.overload_title: An audio callback exceeded its deadline: increase the buffer size (Settings → Audio Output) or lower the polyphony.

status.loading_samples: Loading samples... This may take a moment.

dialogs.sample_folder_title: Select the JM-Rec project folder (or a folder containing sample folders)
dialogs.shutdown_confirm:
Close the software AND shut down the computer?

The current state will be saved first.
dialogs.external_sampleset_title: External sample set — select the main folder (unencrypted .wav files only)
dialogs.export_source_folder_title: Select the sample folder to export

alerts.max_midi_signals: Maximum 4 MIDI signals per coupler/stop button

toolbar.bar_title: Show main bar (tabs, profile switch, audio start/stop)
toolbar.rec_audio_start: Start MP3 recording (what you hear) into Documents\JM-Orgue-opnames
toolbar.rec_midi_running: MIDI recording — {n} events · {t} · Click to stop
toolbar.rec_midi_start: Start MIDI recording (what you play — notes only); saved in Documents\JM-Orgue-opnames
toolbar.play_recording_title: Load the MIDI you just recorded into the player and play it back (draw the stops yourself)
toolbar.notate_title: Open the notation window: play live and see the notes appear as you play (layers, overdub, rhythm tolerance, editing); you can also open an existing MIDI file there
toolbar.shutdown_title: Close the software AND shut down the computer · right-click or hold 3s = MIDI learn
toolbar.couplers_to_bar: Show couplers in their own bar
toolbar.couplers_to_division: Show couplers as knobs within the division

sampleset.loops_confirm: Detect loops and write them into the WAV files? The originals are backed up to a "_loopbackup" folder first.

feedback.title: Feedback (MIDI out)
feedback.desc: Let the physical console light up with the registration: stop lamps (Note On/Off), a Hauptwerk text display, or a Johannus/Content console.
feedback.base_note_hint: Each stop automatically gets a note number starting from the base note (stop order), or learn the real console button per stop:
feedback.learn_prompt: Now press the corresponding stop button on your console… (20 s)
feedback.active_desc: — the console follows every stop change, preset and tutti.
feedback.inactive_hint: Choose a port and click "Apply" to connect.

about.title: About & feedback
about.copyright: © Martijn van der Kolk, all rights reserved. The code may not be used without permission.
about.send_feedback_title: Send a message that reaches the author directly (by e-mail)
about.github_title: Opens the GitHub issues page in your browser
about.feedback_privacy: Your message goes directly to the author. Only what you enter below, the version number and the organ name are sent — plus the log if you leave that checked below.
about.feedback_hobby: Please note: JM-Orgue is a hobby project — a reply may therefore take a few days. Thank you in advance for your patience!
about.feedback_placeholder: What would you like to report? (bug, wish, question…)
about.feedback_email_placeholder: Your e-mail address (optional — for a reply)
about.feedback_include_log: Include log file (technical log of this and the previous session — helps to track down errors)
about.feedback_failed: Sending failed (no internet?). Try again later or use the GitHub button.
about.feedback_no_endpoint: The mail route is not yet configured in this version — please use the GitHub button for now.

audio.profile_device_unavailable: {label}: device "{device}" is not available right now (is it switched on / connected?). The current output stays active.
audio.headphones_profile_not_set: The Headphones profile has not been set up yet. First choose the headphone output (host, device and optionally channels) under Settings → Audio Output and save it as Headphones; after that this button switches directly.
audio.switch_taking_long: The audio switch is taking longer than expected — please wait a moment.
audio.overload_warn: The audio thread is missing its deadline (peak {peak}% of the buffer time at {frames} frames). You hear this as clicks or stutter on stop and crescendo changes.
audio.asio_restart_advice: The ASIO driver '{device}' cannot be restarted in this session. JM-Orgue is now playing through {host}. Restart JM-Orgue to restore ASIO; your registration is kept.
audio.asio_restart_confirm: JM-Orgue will close and restart to restore the ASIO driver. Your settings and registration are saved first. Continue?

pistons.learn_desc: Learn fixed console buttons (pistons): general cancel, SET, preset steps, memory levels, shut down computer, etc. The number buttons 0–9 are learned on the combination bar itself (right-click or hold for 3 s).
pistons.learn_prompt: Now press the desired button on your console… (20 s)

recording.midi_no_notes: No notes recorded — play on the keyboard (via MIDI) during the recording.

midi_archive.title: Automatic MIDI archive
midi_archive.subtitle: Silently captures everything you play as a .mid file: starts at the first note, stops after silence. Notes only — draw the stops yourself when playing back.
midi_archive.enabled_title: On: every playing session is saved automatically as .mid in the archive folder. Off: manual MIDI recording only.
midi_archive.limits_title: Silence: the file is closed after this many seconds without a key press. Min. notes / min. length: shorter takes (an accidental key press) are not kept.

notation.open_failed: Could not open the notation window.
notation.open_failed_error: Could not open the notation window: {error}
notation.wizard_hint: Choose how many staves you want, with which clef, and which divisions go to which staff while you play. Several takes layered on one staff can be added afterwards via the layer bar.
notation.no_organ_routing_later: no organ loaded — routing can be set later
notation.wizard_has_notes: There are already notes — the layout can only be replaced while the score is empty.
notation.record_start_title: Start recording — begins at the first note
notation.play_title: Play the score through the organ (current registration)
notation.tempo_test_title: Click one bar to hear the tempo (records nothing)
notation.metronome_title: Metronome click in the notation window (separate click, no organ pipe)
notation.count_in_title: Number of beats to count in before recording starts
notation.step_input_title: Step input: play a key or chord on the keyboard — or click on the staff — and the note is placed at the input cursor with the chosen value
notation.title: Title
notation.tolerance_title: Drag left for literal (loose), right for tight (hard quantisation)
notation.open_import_title: Import an existing MIDI file as extra take(s) into this score
notation.save_as_midi_title: Save the score (visible takes) as a MIDI file
notation.layer_armed_title: This staff is armed — recording writes here
notation.take_visible_title: Show take in the notation? Several visible takes together = overdub on this staff
notation.layer_divisions_title: Which divisions route to this staff while playing
notation.count_in_suffix_one: beat to go — play on beat 1.
notation.count_in_suffix_many: beats to go — play on beat 1.
notation.selected_many: notes selected — click a note (Shift+click = several), or arrows ←/→.
notation.selection_detail: (note {i} of {total}, staff "{layer}") — click a note to select it.
notation.click_to_select: Click a note in the score to select it, or use ←/→.
notation.empty_score: No notes in the score yet — press Record and play.
notation.hint_live: Tip: Record = play, each division on its own staff; ▶ plays the score through the organ. Step input (N): play a key/chord, type A–G (Shift = chord), or click on the staff; 2–7 = value, . dot, 0 rest, R repeat, ↑/↓ sharp/flat, Backspace back. Correcting: click/←→ to select, drag a note up/down for pitch, ↑/↓ transpose, Shift+←/→ shift in time, Delete, [ ÷2, ] ×2, Ctrl+C/V, Ctrl+Z.
notation.hint_file: Tip: played freely? Set the tempo you played at and slide "Rhythm" towards loose if the quantisation feels too tight.

eq.channel_note: EQ works per output channel, after the reverb — choose "All channels" or a specific channel per band.

reverb.fixed_room_hint: Fixed room sound. Choose "Custom (per organ)" to set RT60, pre-delay, damping and room size yourself — that setting is saved with this organ.
reverb.recorded_room_hint: This sample set already carries the church acoustics in the sound ({n} pipes with a release recording). Extra reverb here is a matter of taste, not necessity — too much makes it muddy.

learn.pedal_timeout_low: No pedal movement received (20 s time-out). Move the pedal to its lowest position and hold it still there.
learn.pedal_timeout_high: No highest position received (20 s time-out).
learn.pedal_range_too_small: The lowest and highest positions are too close together (fewer than 8 CC steps). Move the pedal from fully closed to fully open and try again.
learn.key_timeout_second: No second key received (20 s time-out).
learn.key_channel_mismatch: The second key came in on MIDI channel {second} instead of {first} — press both keys on the same manual.
learn.pedal_low_prompt: Move the pedal to the LOWEST position (closed) and hold it still…
learn.pedal_high_prompt: Now move the pedal to the HIGHEST position (open) and hold it still…
learn.key_low_prompt: Now press the LOWEST key of this keyboard…

bindings.choose_target_first: Choose a target for the new binding first.
bindings.editor_intro: All MIDI bindings of this organ in one list. Change type, channel or number directly, remove a binding with ✕, or add one manually at the bottom — learning keeps working alongside. Channel 'All' = responds on every channel. For CC: activates as soon as the value ≥ the threshold.
bindings.threshold_title: Activates as soon as the CC value ≥ this threshold
bindings.empty: No MIDI bindings yet — learn them, or add one manually below.
bindings.threshold_new_title: Threshold: activates as soon as the CC value ≥ this
bindings.reload_title: Reload the list (e.g. after learning via the buttons)

wind.groups_count_title: Number of wind supplies / chests. Default = each division its own.
wind.group_title: Wind group: divisions in the same group share one wind reservoir
wind.group_select_title: Choose a wind group. The same number for two divisions = shared reservoir (e.g. pedal separate, 2 manuals together).

crescendo.shrink_confirm: Fewer steps ({old} → {new}): the stops in the steps above {new} will be lost. Continue?
crescendo.autofill_title: Distribute all stops automatically over the steps (ascending)
crescendo.editor_hint_click: Click a cell = stop on/off in that step
crescendo.manual_title: Manual: MIDI channel and CC number of the crescendo pedal (alternative to learning)
crescendo.invert_title: Invert: reverses the pedal direction (handy if the pedal works the other way round)
crescendo.range_title: Manual CC range of the crescendo pedal (0–127). Min = off, Max = full.
crescendo.binding_disabled_warn: A crescendo pedal has been learned (channel {channel} · CC{cc}), but the general crescendo is switched off. That pedal now does nothing — not even as a swell box, because the CC stays reserved for the crescendo.
crescendo.binding_empty_warn: A crescendo pedal has been learned (channel {channel} · CC{cc}), but no steps have been filled in yet. Use Auto-fill or the matrix, otherwise the pedal does nothing.

ccis.global_title: Global C/C# chest spread — applies per keyboard where you enable the spread below.
ccis.global_desc: — C (and D, E, …) to one side, C# (and D#, F, …) to the other
ccis.strength_title: How strongly the two chests are separated (0% = mono, 95% = almost fully L/R)
ccis.falloff_title: How quickly the spread merges towards the treble (0% = still just as strong at the top, 100% = fully mono at the top — like a real organ)
ccis.swap_title: Swap which side is C and which is C#
ccis.division_title: C/C# chest spread: even notes sound to one side, odd notes to the other — like a real organ with separate C and C# chests. Strongly separated for the (lowest) notes, merging more and more towards the treble.

swell.manual_title: Manual: MIDI channel and CC number of the swell pedal (alternative to learning)
swell.invert_title: Invert: reverses the pedal direction (handy if the pedal works the other way round)
swell.range_title: Manual CC range of the swell pedal (0–127). Min = closed, Max = open.

update.dismiss_title: Don't show this notice again for this version
update.up_to_date: You are using the latest version.
update.check_failed: Check failed. No internet connection? Please try again later.
update.install_now_title: Downloads the update, closes JM-Orgue and restarts it automatically
update.installing: Installing update — JM-Orgue will restart shortly…
update.failed: Update failed: {error}. You can also download the update yourself.
update.confirm_install: JM-Orgue will close to install the update and restart automatically afterwards. Your current settings are saved first. Continue?
update.macos_manual: On macOS you update manually: download the dmg and reinstall the app (automatic updating is not possible because the app is not signed by Apple).

general.autostart_title: JM-Orgue starts automatically after sign-in. Handy on a dedicated console PC.
general.auto_load_last_organ: Automatically load the last opened organ at startup
general.auto_load_last_organ_title: On: the last opened organ is loaded automatically when the app starts. Off: the app opens with the organ selection.
general.restore_registration: Restore the last registration when opening
general.restore_registration_title: On: when an organ is opened, the last drawn stops come back. Off: clean start (no stops on).

remote.enable_title: On: JM-Orgue listens on all network adapters. Open the address or scan the QR code on a tablet or phone in the same (Wi-Fi) network to control stops, couplers, tremulant, setzer and volume remotely. Off: no network access.
remote.new_token_confirm: Create a new token? Previously scanned QR codes and saved addresses will stop working.
remote.url_label: Address for tablet/phone (or scan the QR code):
remote.no_lan_ip: No network address found — is this PC connected to Wi-Fi or a network cable?
remote.hint: The first time, Windows Firewall asks whether JM-Orgue may accept connections: choose 'Allow access' for private networks. Declined it? Enable it via Windows Security → Firewall → 'Allow an app through firewall' (JM-Orgue, Private). The address only works inside your own (Wi-Fi) network and is not encrypted; do not share the token and create a new token to revoke access.
remote.parts_title: Parts shown on the remote screen
remote.parts_hint: For the rest the remote screen follows the organ screen: the same order of divisions and stops, the same knob shape and the same couplers. Choose which couplers are visible under Organ settings → Couplers; the remote screen never shows more than the organ screen.

pedal.taken_over: This pedal was already assigned to {what}; that assignment has been taken over. One pedal can only have one function.
pedal.cc_required: Enter a CC number as well — selecting only a channel does not create an assignment.
